artists.biography: Shakespears Sister are a British-based pop-rock band formed by Irish-born singer-songwriter Siobhan Fahey in 1988, with plaudits including a BRIT Award and Ivor Novello Award. It was Fahey's first musical outing since leaving Bananarama, and initially a solo project. American backing vocalist and guitarist Marcella Detroit began working with Fahey in 1989 which led to a partnership and Shakespears Sister became a duo as of their 1989 hit single "You're History". After a string of hit singles and two successful albums, tensions between Fahey and Detroit led to a split in 1993. Fahey resumed as the sole member until 1996. In 2009, after a 13-year hiatus, Fahey resurrected the band to release a new album, Songs from the Red Room.

perplexity.description:
Released in 1992 on London Records, Hormonally Yours is the second studio album by Shakespears Sister and stands as a defining work in their discography. The album blends rock and pop with a distinctive blend of dramatic melodies, lush harmonies, and emotionally charged lyrics, reflecting the group’s evolution from a solo project led by Siobhan Fahey into a dynamic duo with Marcella Detroit. Musically, the album is characterized by its atmospheric production, strong vocal performances, and genre-blurring tracks that range from brooding ballads to energetic pop-rock anthems.

Hormonally Yours achieved significant commercial success, reaching No. 3 on the UK Albums Chart and earning double platinum status. It is best known for the hit single "Stay," which became a chart-topping success and remains one of the most iconic pop songs of the early 1990s. The album solidified Shakespears Sister’s reputation as a major force in British pop-rock, marking a high point in their career and distinguishing itself with its bold artistic vision and memorable songwriting.
